title: Publish the Yazelix family root and Eon site when ready
description:
## Why
Yazelix is the established product family. Yazelix Nova and Yazelix Eon are parallel product lines with similar user-facing goals and different architectures. When Eon has an accepted public site, the apex can present that family without moving Nova or making either line appear deprecated.

## Accepted Decision
- Public product names are **Yazelix Nova** and **Yazelix Eon**.
- Eon came after Nova chronologically; that does not make it a replacement or make Nova legacy.
- Both lines are intended to evolve in parallel.
- The already-owned `yazelix.com` domain is sufficient; no additional registered domain is required.
- **Yazelix Nova launches and remains canonical at `https://nova.yazelix.com`.**
- There is no Nova-at-root phase, later Nova move, or established apex URL set that must be redirected to Nova.
- After Yazelix Eon has an accepted public site and the user activates this issue:
  - `https://yazelix.com` becomes a concise Yazelix family landing page;
  - `https://eon.yazelix.com` becomes the canonical Yazelix Eon site;
  - `https://nova.yazelix.com` continues unchanged as the canonical Yazelix Nova site.
- Any separately purchased Yazelix Nova or Yazelix Eon domain is defensive/redirect-only unless a later explicit decision changes this contract.

## Scope
In:
- Trigger only after the Nova launch is complete and Yazelix Eon has an accepted public website.
- Publish a small family chooser that explains the shared Yazelix promise and the two architectural lines without ranking one as the replacement.
- Connect the independently owned Eon site at `eon.yazelix.com`.
- Configure DNS, TLS, sitemap/canonical metadata, and cross-links for the apex and Eon hosts.
- Verify that the existing Nova host, paths, canonical metadata, documentation truth, release evidence, and deployment owner remain unchanged.
- Verify that each product keeps its own documentation, release truth, and deployment owner while sharing the Yazelix brand.

Out:
- Building Yazelix Eon, writing its documentation, merging the two site codebases, or creating shared runtime/release policy.
- Buying a second domain as a prerequisite.
- Moving Nova, changing Nova canonical URLs, creating apex-to-Nova migration redirects, or merging product documentation.
- Executing activation before both the family copy and Eon site are accepted.

External contract:
- A visitor to `yazelix.com` can choose between Yazelix Nova and Yazelix Eon.
- `nova.yazelix.com` remains the stable Nova origin before and after family activation.
- `eon.yazelix.com` owns Eon.
- Neither product page describes the other as obsolete, legacy, or its release successor.

## Implementation Notes
- Keep the family landing page static and minimal.
- Prefer independent product deployments behind subdomains; share no documentation source of truth.
- Reuse visual brand assets directly where accepted, but do not create a shared theme package until repeated maintenance demonstrates a need.
- The Nova hosting decision only needs to permit independent future apex/Eon hosting; it does not need migration or redirect machinery.

## Verification
- The user explicitly activates this work after accepting the public Yazelix Eon site and family copy.
- DNS and valid TLS resolve for the apex, `nova`, and `eon` hosts.
- Nova routes and canonical URLs are identical before and after activation; no redirect loop or unintended recanonicalization is introduced.
- Apex and Eon canonical tags, sitemap entries, robots behavior, navigation, and social metadata name the correct host/product.
- Desktop/mobile and keyboard checks pass for the family landing page.
- Both product sites independently pass their release checks.

## Stop Conditions
- Stop while Yazelix Eon remains private, alpha-only, or lacks accepted public content.
- Stop if activation would require moving or recanonicalizing Nova.
- Do not make this bead a prerequisite for the Nova launch.
- Do not merge product documentation merely because the products share a brand.

## Maintenance
- Status: deferred until the trigger above.
- Effort: M.
- Risk: MEDIUM because apex/Eon DNS and public identity are user-facing, but Nova has no migration.
- Confidence: HIGH in the permanent Nova domain model; implementation timing depends on Yazelix Eon public readiness.
- Reconsideration trigger: an explicit user decision changing the Yazelix family/product naming or canonical domain strategy.

title: Launch an accurate Yazelix Nova website at nova.yazelix.com
description:
## Why
Yazelix needs one public, accurate Nova site at its permanent canonical host, `https://nova.yazelix.com`. The canonical Yazelix repository owns the public product launch decision and source links; this site repository owns the static implementation and its launch evidence.

## Evidence
- `src/pages/index.astro` and several task/reference pages still contain Classic-era claims that Nova does not own.
- `tests/site-smoke.spec.ts` can pass while product claims are stale because it primarily checks rendering and route shape.
- `astro.config.mjs`, `public/robots.txt`, `README.md`, and `docs/site_shape.md` currently name the apex `yazelix.com`; these are stale against the permanent-domain decision.
- On 2026-08-08, `https://yazelix.com` resolved to a Hostinger parked-domain page and the GitHub repository had no Pages configuration.
- Canonical product issue: `yazelix-launch-yazelix-website-ten4-pgh` in the Yazelix repository.

## Product Family Boundary
- Yazelix is the established product family. **Yazelix Nova** and **Yazelix Eon** are parallel lines with similar product goals and different architectures.
- Eon came after Nova chronologically; neither line supersedes the other, and both are intended to evolve.
- **Permanent rule:** Yazelix Nova launches at `https://nova.yazelix.com` and remains canonical there. There is no Nova-at-root phase and no later Nova host migration.
- The existing `yazelix.com` registration owns the namespace; no additional registered domain is required.
- Deferred issue `yazelix-site-activate-yazelix-family-domains-v8d` may later publish a family landing page at the apex and Yazelix Eon at `eon.yazelix.com`, but it must not move or recanonicalize Nova.

## Scope
In:
- Deliver the child outcomes for product truth, dependency safety, honest media, permanent-host metadata/accessibility, Blog scope, hosting, and production cutover.
- Keep Astro + Starlight and the static-site boundary unless a child records evidence that this is impossible.
- Make `nova.yazelix.com` the single canonical host in site configuration, metadata, sitemap, robots, documentation identity, DNS, TLS, and production proof.
- Verify the installed public site, not only the source tree.

Out:
- A backend, CMS, analytics platform, user accounts, or dynamic application runtime.
- The separate Beads-viewer product decision.
- Recreating Yazelix Classic compatibility or its old capture backlog.
- An apex-first launch, temporary root canonical, or future Nova-domain migration.

External contract:
- A visitor opening `nova.yazelix.com` can understand Nova, install or try the supported channel, configure/update/recover it, inspect current keybindings and workspace behavior, and reach canonical project sources.
- Every Nova canonical URL remains on `https://nova.yazelix.com`; later family/Eon publication does not change those URLs.
- Broken deployment must fail visibly and preserve a documented rollback path.

## Implementation Notes
- Treat the exact accepted revision of the canonical Yazelix README, architecture, docs, and assets as source evidence; record that revision in the content/media work.
- Prefer deletion of stale claims and media over translating the entire Classic site.
- Keep the launch chain thin: static build -> chosen host -> `nova` DNS/TLS.
- Do not add redirects for a Nova apex phase that never existed.

## Verification
- Every launch-gating child issue is closed with its own evidence.
- `bun run check`, `bun run build`, and `bun run test:e2e` pass at the candidate revision.
- Built HTML, sitemap, robots, and social/canonical metadata use `https://nova.yazelix.com` and contain no Nova canonical claim for bare `https://yazelix.com`.
- A fresh public check confirms TLS and the core routes `/`, `/start/`, `/configure/`, `/update/`, `/recover/`, `/keybindings/`, `/docs/`, and `/features/` on the Nova subdomain.
- Critical outbound project links resolve to the intended canonical repositories.

## Stop Conditions
- Stop for the user if hosting or Blog scope is still undecided.
- Stop if DNS authority for `nova.yazelix.com` cannot be verified.
- Stop if a proposed claim is not supported by a named canonical source.
- Do not add dynamic infrastructure to solve a static-site requirement.

## Maintenance
- Effort: L overall.
- Risk: MEDIUM because public DNS/cutover and stale product claims are user-facing.
- Confidence: HIGH that the current stack can deliver the permanent Nova subdomain without a rewrite.
- Replacement cost: low while the site remains static; avoid provider-specific application code.

title: Patch the vulnerable Astro build toolchain
description:
## Why
The site build must not ship or develop against a dependency graph with known high-severity advisories. The build remains static; this issue owns only dependency safety and compatibility, not a framework migration for its own sake.

## Evidence
- `package.json:15-23` directly owns Astro, Starlight, Sharp, Astro Check, Playwright, and TypeScript.
- `bun.lock:36` resolves Starlight 0.40.0 against Astro 6.4.x.
- `bun outdated` on 2026-08-08 reported Astro 6.4.5 (7.2.0 latest), Starlight 0.40.0 (0.41.7), Sharp 0.34.5 (0.35.3), Astro Check 0.9.9 (0.9.10), and Playwright 1.60.0 (1.62.1).
- `bun audit` on site revision `b7b3b17` reported 18 advisories: 11 high, 5 moderate, and 2 low. Directly relevant affected packages include Astro <6.4.6 and Sharp <0.35.0; vulnerable transitives include PostCSS, nanoid, SVGO, js-yaml, fast-uri, YAML, and esbuild.

## Scope
In:
- Update the smallest compatible set of direct requirements and `bun.lock` needed to clear high-severity advisories.
- Take current supported Astro/Starlight releases when they reduce net maintenance and the existing pages/tests prove compatibility.
- Record any remaining advisory with its reachability and approved exception.

Out:
- Replacing Astro/Starlight, adding a frontend framework, or redesigning pages.
- Adding automated dependency bots or a broad version policy.

External contract:
- A clean install can check, build, and test the same static routes and behavior without known unaccepted high-severity advisories.

## Implementation Notes
- Try a compatible lock refresh first; cross a major version only where needed for a supported, secure graph.
- Use the existing Bun scripts. Do not introduce a second package manager.
- Review Astro and Starlight migration notes for the exact versions selected; remove obsolete direct dependencies only if the build proves they no longer own behavior.

## Verification
- From a clean dependency install: `bun run check`, `bun run build`, and `bun run test:e2e` pass.
- `bun audit` reports no high-severity finding, or each remaining finding has a specific accepted reachability exception.
- Route count, Pagefind output, sitemap output, and representative desktop/mobile screenshots do not regress.

## Stop Conditions
- Stop if clearing an advisory requires changing public site behavior or adding an adapter layer.
- Stop for review before accepting an advisory exception.
- Do not chase unrelated latest majors after the security and compatibility contract is met.

## Maintenance
- Effort: M.
- Risk: MEDIUM because Astro major changes can affect Starlight and content rendering.
- Confidence: HIGH that an in-place upgrade is sufficient.
- Replacement cost: low; dependencies remain conventional package requirements and one lockfile.

title: Replace Classic copy with the canonical Nova contract
description:
## Accepted Outcome
The homepage and eight task/reference documents describe Yazelix Nova from canonical source revision `37f36efcabf16c41d03e182917926e7b8e56139c`. Public copy covers Stable try/install, `yzx launch` through Mars, `yzx enter` in the current terminal or SSH, channels, package variants, sparse config, native files, Home Manager ownership, updates, doctor/status recovery, and the current workspace key grid.

## Product Contract
- Yazelix remains the master brand; this site is specifically Yazelix Nova.
- `https://nova.yazelix.com` is the permanent Nova site, not a temporary migration host.
- Yazelix Nova and Yazelix Eon are parallel product lines with separate architecture, documentation truth, and release evidence.
- This site does not publish Eon instructions or imply that either line replaces the other.

## Runtime Contract
- Stable install: `nix profile add --refresh github:luccahuguet/yazelix/stable`.
- Stable try routes: `nix run github:luccahuguet/yazelix/stable -- launch` and `nix run github:luccahuguet/yazelix/stable#yazelix-no-mars -- enter`.
- `yzx launch` is the Mars route; `yzx enter` uses the current interactive terminal and works without Mars or a display server.
- Root config is optional sparse `~/.config/yazelix/config.toml`; native component files live under `~/.config/yazelix/`; generated state lives under `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/yazelix` by default.
- Profile and Home Manager installs retain separate update owners. Open sessions retain their immutable Nix store paths until relaunched.
- Recovery starts with argument-free `yzx doctor`; `yzx status`, `yzx status --json`, and `yzx --version` expose runtime identity. Doctor reports Classic residue without modifying it.

## Sources of Truth
- Canonical `README.md`: public product, commands, packages, channels, and keybindings.
- `docs/installation.md`: install, update, channel, package, and Home Manager contracts.
- `docs/configuration.md`: semantic settings and owner-native files.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`: runtime and ownership boundaries.
- `runtime/yzx/cli.rs`, `doctor.rs`, `status.rs`, and `paths.rs`: executable CLI, recovery, status, and path behavior.
- `crates/yzx-config/src/catalog.rs` and `defaults/zellij/config.kdl`: current keybinding catalog and runtime owner.

## Boundaries
Blog essays, the visual gallery, canonical deployment metadata, and a future Yazelix family/Eon site remain outside this issue. Deep volatile tables remain in the canonical repository and are linked from the task pages.

## Verification Evidence
- Unsupported Classic command/path scan returned no matches across `src`, `README.md`, and `docs/site_shape.md`.
- `README.md` and `docs/site_shape.md` identify `https://nova.yazelix.com` as permanent and contain no later-migration promise.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `bun run check`: 15 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 hints.
- `bun run build`: 16 pages built; Pagefind and sitemap completed.
- `bun run test:e2e`: 30/30 Chromium and Pixel 7 checks passed on a fresh dev server.
- All five canonical GitHub links returned HTTP 200.
- Installed Yazelix Nova 1.0.0-beta.5 confirmed `yzx --version`, `yzx status --json`, and argument-free `yzx doctor`, including config/state paths, managed key defaults, package ownership, and read-only Classic-residue warnings.

## Maintenance
Re-audit this copy when a canonical public command, path, package, keybinding, channel, or product-line contract changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Homepage and task/reference docs identify the product line as Yazelix Nova.
- [x] Stable try/install, launch/enter, channels, package variants, config, update, recovery, and keybinding claims match the recorded canonical revision.
- [x] Stale Classic commands, paths, pane claims, and compatibility guidance are absent from the changed public surfaces.
- [x] README and site shape name `https://nova.yazelix.com` as the permanent Nova host and preserve Yazelix as the master brand.
- [x] Canonical detail links resolve.
- [x] Astro diagnostics, production build, and 30 desktop/mobile browser checks pass.
close_reason: Canonical Nova copy, product naming, domain decision, and verification evidence are complete.

title: Guard Nova content and internal link integrity
description:
## Accepted Outcome
The existing Playwright suite contains one public Nova contract test. It reads the homepage and combined docs page, protects the durable Stable install/try commands and sparse config path, rejects an explicit set of Classic-only markers, checks five canonical GitHub destinations syntactically, and walks every reachable same-origin route and fragment target without external network access.

## Observable Contract
- Missing `nix profile add --refresh github:luccahuguet/yazelix/stable`, Stable `launch`, Stable no-Mars `enter`, or `~/.config/yazelix/config.toml` fails with the missing invariant in the assertion message.
- Reintroduced Classic settings paths, obsolete `yzx` commands, doctor flags, version flag, or right-sidebar claim fail the normal browser suite.
- Every same-origin anchor reachable from `/` must return a successful response. Every fragment must identify an element on its target page.
- The existing representative desktop/mobile route list must remain reachable through site navigation.
- Canonical external destinations are asserted as URLs only; ordinary tests never depend on GitHub availability.

## Implementation
- `tests/site-smoke.spec.ts` owns the single contract/link walk and retains the existing Playwright runner and two projects.
- Fixed media, docs, and Blog content-count assertions were replaced with behavior and destination checks.
- `src/pages/docs/index.astro` prefixes all rendered documentation heading IDs and their Starlight anchor links at the existing combined-docs render boundary. Only level-two headings participate in rail activation.
- No dependency, crawler framework, test runner, snapshot, or external uptime check was added.

## Material Finding
The first link-integrity run found that `/docs/` prefixed rendered heading IDs but left Starlight heading-anchor `href` values unprefixed. Links such as `/docs/#install` therefore targeted no element. The accepted fix updates both halves at the existing render boundary; weakening fragment validation was rejected.

## Verification Evidence
- Temporary mutation of the protected no-Mars Stable command failed with `missing public Nova contract: nix run github:luccahuguet/yazelix/stable#yazelix-no-mars -- enter` on Chromium and Pixel 7.
- Temporary mutation of the homepage Features destination to `/missing/` failed with `broken internal link: /missing/` on both projects.
- Both temporary mutations were reverted before final verification.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `bun run check`: 15 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 hints.
- `bun run build`: 16 pages built; Pagefind and sitemap completed.
- `bun run test:e2e`: 32/32 Chromium and Pixel 7 tests passed.

## Maintenance
Change protected strings only when the canonical public Nova contract changes. Keep internal-link checks network-independent and extend the representative route list only for a public surface that is not reachable from existing navigation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] One existing-runner test protects Stable install/try, launch/enter, config path, critical canonical destinations, and Classic-only exclusions.
- [x] Every reachable same-origin route and fragment target is validated without a new dependency or external request.
- [x] Fixed media, docs, and Blog counts no longer own content policy.
- [x] Combined-docs heading IDs and anchor destinations share the same prefix owner.
- [x] Temporary command and broken-href mutations produced the intended actionable failures and were reverted.
- [x] Astro diagnostics, production build, and 32 desktop/mobile browser checks pass.
close_reason: Nova content drift and internal route/fragment integrity are protected by the normal Playwright suite.

title: Replace the Classic gallery with a lean Nova product tour
description:
## Outcome
The launch site presents Yazelix Nova through one maintained workspace image and four focused, honest views. The 26-item Classic catalog, obsolete Classic hero, animated media, placeholders, and duplicated near-1 MB logo are removed.

## Accepted contract
- Consumer: visitors to the homepage and features page.
- Trigger: load either product-tour surface.
- Result: see the full Nova workspace plus focused files/editor, runtime-status, and keyboard-map views, each with a caption and exact docs link.
- Failure/fallback: meaningful alt text and captions preserve the explanation when images are unavailable; no motion is required.
- Owners: `src/data/feature_media.ts` owns tour content and focus metadata; `FeatureMediaFrame.astro` owns static rendering; the canonical Yazelix repository owns product truth.

## Accepted implementation
- All four views reuse `/images/nova_workspace.png`; CSS crops provide focus without duplicate downloads.
- Static PNG rendering uses intrinsic dimensions, lazy loading outside the hero, asynchronous decoding, alt text, and captions.
- The homepage shows three previews; `/features/` shows the complete four-view tour.
- Removed 29 Classic gallery files (2,362,374 bytes), the 431,839-byte Classic hero, and the 997,705-byte duplicate logo.
- Starlight and the custom navigation reuse the existing 54,905-byte favicon; no dependency was added.
- `docs/site_shape.md` records provenance and admits future media only when it explains a stable public behavior better than text.

## Source evidence
- Canonical Nova revision: `37f36efcabf16c41d03e182917926e7b8e56139c`.
- Canonical source: `assets/screenshots/nova_workspace.png`.
- SHA-256 in canonical source, `public/`, and built `dist/`: `f476451f01b4ebd2bf773369981ed5d571865b6bbf26d8cbc6f27b32df364b71`.

## Acceptance evidence
Verified on 2026-08-08 from site worktree base `b7b3b1700925a9e30c74aa14949cacada9616563`, Bun 1.3.13:
- `bun run check`: 15 files, zero errors, warnings, or hints.
- `bun run build`: 16 pages built successfully with Pagefind and sitemap.
- `bun run test:e2e`: 30/30 tests passed across desktop and Pixel 7 projects.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- Headless browser checks: every homepage/features image loaded; all Nova images have alt text; the first 12 keyboard targets were reachable and visible.
- Visual inspection passed for desktop, Pixel 7, `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, and image-disabled fallback; captions keep all four views understandable without media.
- No GIF, MP4, WebM, Classic gallery path, or “Capture planned” placeholder remains in source or built public output.
- Public assets: 3,846,894 -> 526,260 bytes (86.3% smaller).
- Built site: 6,112,889 -> 1,839,559 bytes (69.9% smaller).
- Largest built asset is the 471,284-byte Nova screenshot; no identical near-1 MB logo copies remain.

## Scope held
No GUI runtime capture, motion player, new dependency, media CMS, or speculative capture backlog was added. Add a separate capture only after a stable Nova behavior needs motion or a distinct state to be explained honestly.
acceptance_criteria:
Complete when:
- Homepage and features page show current Nova evidence from the recorded canonical revision.
- The launch tour contains one maintained workspace view and three focused high-value views, all backed by one static asset.
- Every view has meaningful alt text, a caption, and a docs link and remains understandable without images or motion.
- No Classic-only gallery media, placeholder, GIF, MP4, or WebM ships.
- No identical near-1 MB logo copies ship.
- Check, build, 30-case end-to-end suite, desktop/mobile/reduced-motion/image-disabled inspection, and byte-inventory comparison pass.
close_reason: Accepted: lean Nova tour implemented and fully verified

title: Complete metadata and keyboard access on custom pages
description:
## Accepted Outcome
The permanent Nova origin is `https://nova.yazelix.com`. Astro configuration owns that origin for sitemap generation and Starlight metadata; `public/robots.txt` names the matching sitemap. Five custom route shapes share one native `SiteHead.astro` owner for document basics, canonical URLs, Open Graph fields, Twitter card fields, favicon, and the accepted Nova workspace image.

## Metadata Contract
- Homepage, Features, combined Docs, Blog index, and Blog post routes each emit exactly one description and one absolute canonical URL derived from `Astro.site` plus the request pathname.
- Open Graph owns type, Yazelix site name, title, description, URL, and the 1864x1012 PNG image with honest alt text.
- Twitter owns a large-image card, title, description, image, and matching alt text.
- Blog posts use Open Graph type `article`; the remaining custom routes use `website`.
- The accepted social image is `/images/nova_workspace.png`; no second image owner or generated placeholder exists.
- Standalone documentation pages remain owned by Starlight. Changing `Astro.site` gives their native canonical metadata the Nova origin without replacing Starlight internals.

## Keyboard Contract
`SiteNav.astro` emits the first focusable link, `Skip to content`, on every custom page. Each custom page owns one `<main id="main-content" tabindex="-1">`. Tab reveals a fixed, high-contrast skip control; Enter updates the fragment and moves focus to main content. The 120 ms transition is removed when reduced motion is requested.

## Implementation
- Added `src/components/SiteHead.astro` and replaced five duplicated partial heads.
- Added the shared skip link to `SiteNav.astro`, one main target per custom route, and focused styling in the existing `home.css` owner.
- Updated `astro.config.mjs` and `public/robots.txt` to the permanent Nova host.
- Added one existing-runner browser test covering metadata equality, absolute destinations, and first-focus activation across the five custom route shapes.
- No dependency, SEO plugin, layout abstraction, analytics, schema expansion, or Starlight override was added.

## Verification Evidence
- Before implementation, the targeted Chromium and Pixel 7 test failed because custom pages had zero canonical links.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `bun run check`: 16 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 hints.
- `bun run build`: 16 pages built; Pagefind and sitemap completed.
- Static inspection of five built custom routes found one description, one canonical, all required Open Graph/Twitter fields, and Nova-rooted absolute URLs. The built `/start/` Starlight canonical also uses Nova.
- Built `robots.txt`, sitemap index, and sitemap route entries use `https://nova.yazelix.com`; no `https://yazelix.com` crawl or canonical origin remains in config, public assets, or build output.
- `bun run test:e2e`: 34/34 Chromium and Pixel 7 tests passed.
- Desktop 1440x900 and mobile 412x915 visual probes showed the focused skip link fully visible at `(12, 12)`, with dark text on a pale green background and a green 3 px outline. Enter focused `#main-content` on every tested route.

## Maintenance
When a custom route is added, use `SiteHead` and give its main landmark the shared target. If the Blog boundary removes Blog routes, remove those consumers and test cases without changing the shared contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Astro, robots, sitemap, custom canonicals, and native Starlight canonicals use `https://nova.yazelix.com`.
- [x] Five custom route shapes emit one description, one canonical, complete Open Graph/Twitter fields, and the accepted Nova image.
- [x] Every custom page exposes a first-focus visible skip link that focuses its main landmark.
- [x] Desktop and mobile visual inspection confirms the focused control is visible and does not break page composition.
- [x] No plugin, dependency, schema expansion, analytics, or Starlight override was added.
- [x] Astro diagnostics, production build, static metadata inspection, and 34 browser checks pass.
close_reason: Permanent Nova metadata and keyboard skip access are complete across all custom route shapes.

title: Choose whether Blog ships at launch
description:
## Why
The site advertises a Blog, but the three current posts are launch-validation prose rather than durable user-facing essays. Shipping them weakens the product; removing Blog is simpler unless real editorial content is part of launch scope.

## Evidence
- `src/components/SiteNav.astro:8-13` makes Blog a primary navigation destination.
- `docs/site_shape.md:99-105` assigns Blog release essays, product reasoning, architecture writing, and lessons.
- `src/content/blog/docs-that-respect-runtime-boundaries.md:2-14` calls itself “A validation post” and talks about what the site should do.
- The other two posts at `src/content/blog/reproducible-terminal-workspace.md:8-14` and `src/content/blog/the-shape-of-a-reproducible-workspace.md:10-14` also describe the intended website rather than adding substantive product knowledge.
- `tests/site-smoke.spec.ts:81-87` protects the count and titles of these placeholders.

## Scope
In:
- Choose and record one launch boundary:
  1. Remove Blog from navigation/routes/content until there is approved writing; or
  2. Keep Blog, delete validation posts, and name the minimum approved substantive post(s) that ship.
- Record the decision owner, rationale, and what would trigger reconsideration.

Out:
- Writing the posts, choosing a CMS, comments, newsletters, feeds, or a long-term editorial calendar.

External contract:
- The launch navigation does not promise an editorial surface filled with placeholder content.

## Implementation Notes
- Recommendation: remove Blog for launch unless the user has a specific approved essay ready.
- The implementation child must follow the recorded choice and must not invent copy to satisfy a route count.

## Verification
- The issue records one explicit option, decision owner, approval date, and named content if Blog remains.
- The dependent implementation issue can be completed without another product-scope guess.

## Stop Conditions
- This is a user/product choice; stop rather than inferring that a placeholder Blog must survive.
- Do not treat “the code already exists” as evidence that Blog belongs in launch scope.

## Maintenance
- Effort: XS.
- Risk: LOW.
- Confidence: HIGH that the current content should not ship unchanged.
- Reconsideration trigger: an approved substantive article and an owner for ongoing accuracy.

title: Apply the chosen launch Blog boundary
description:
## Why
Once the launch Blog boundary is approved, the site must consistently implement it across routes, navigation, content collections, metadata, and tests.

## Evidence
- `src/components/SiteNav.astro:8-13` publishes Blog in primary navigation.
- `src/content.config.ts:9-16` owns the Blog collection.
- `src/pages/blog/index.astro:1-54` and `src/pages/blog/[slug].astro:1-66` own Blog routes.
- `src/content/blog/` contains three validation posts, and `tests/site-smoke.spec.ts:81-87` hard-codes them.
- The parent decision issue owns whether this surface survives launch.

## Scope
In:
- If Blog is removed: delete its nav/route/content/test surface cleanly and remove launch copy that promises it.
- If Blog remains: delete the three validation posts, publish only the specifically approved substantive content, and update route/tests/metadata accordingly.
- Keep content collection code only if a surviving route consumes it.

Out:
- CMS, comments, RSS unless explicitly chosen in the decision, authoring automation, or speculative placeholders for future posts.

External contract:
- Blog navigation and routes exactly match the approved launch decision and contain no validation/staging prose.

## Implementation Notes
- Prefer deletion when the decision is “not at launch.”
- Do not create generic filler content. A retained post needs an approved subject and product-source evidence.
- Keep tests behavioral; do not protect arbitrary post counts.

## Verification
- `bun run check`, `bun run build`, and `bun run test:e2e` pass.
- Search built output for “validation post” and “website should”; no placeholder copy ships.
- Navigation, sitemap, and direct Blog URLs match the chosen boundary, including intentional 404 behavior when removed.

## Stop Conditions
- Stop if the parent decision is not explicit.
- Stop if retained copy makes claims unsupported by canonical sources.
- Do not retain dead collection or route scaffolding “for later.”

## Maintenance
- Effort: S.
- Risk: LOW.
- Confidence: HIGH once the decision is recorded.
- Replacement cost: low; a static Blog can be reintroduced when approved content exists.

title: Choose static hosting for the permanent Nova subdomain
description:
## Why
The repository produces a static site, but no deployment owner exists. Hosting and DNS are consequential ownership choices that must be explicit before publication, and the provider must support Nova's permanent subdomain without creating a later migration.

## Evidence
- `astro.config.mjs` currently declares the stale canonical site `https://yazelix.com`.
- `package.json` builds a static Astro site with Pagefind, sitemap, and `404.html`.
- The site repository has no deployment workflow or provider configuration.
- On 2026-08-08, the apex resolved to a Hostinger parked page and GitHub API returned no Pages configuration.

## Accepted Domain Model
- The existing `yazelix.com` registration owns the family namespace; no additional domain purchase is required.
- **Yazelix Nova launches at `https://nova.yazelix.com` and remains canonical there permanently.**
- There is no Nova-at-root phase, no later host move, and no apex-to-Nova redirect migration to preserve.
- The apex remains available for a future Yazelix family landing page.
- `https://eon.yazelix.com` remains available for a separately owned Yazelix Eon site.
- Any separately registered product-line domain is redirect-only unless the user later changes this contract.
- The remaining decision in this issue is the static host and operational plan, not the domain model.

## Scope
In:
- Choose GitHub Pages, the existing Hostinger account, or another named static host.
- Record the build/deploy trigger, source branch or artifact owner, required credentials, DNS records, TLS ownership, 404 behavior, rollback, and cutover authority.
- Confirm the chosen provider can serve `nova.yazelix.com` now and later serve the apex and `eon.yazelix.com` as independently deployed static sites without moving Nova.
- Prefer the smallest provider-native static path.

Out:
- Implementing deployment or DNS changes, building the future family/Eon sites, dynamic hosting, preview fleets, a CDN abstraction, or multi-provider failover.
- Designing a migration or redirect layer for a Nova-at-root phase that will not exist.

External contract:
- One named system owns publication of the exact Nova artifact at `https://nova.yazelix.com`, and one documented action can roll back or restore the prior known-good artifact without changing its canonical host.

## Implementation Notes
- Recommendation: GitHub Pages remains the smallest likely fit for a public static repository if current account and DNS authority are confirmed.
- Hostinger remains valid only if its existing operational ownership is intentionally preferred and it can independently bind the required hosts.
- Cloudflare Pages remains credible when Cloudflare DNS/CDN ownership is already desired.
- Compare actual account access and DNS authority, not brand preference.

## Verification
- The issue records one provider, exact source/trigger, required secret/permission set, `nova` DNS/TLS steps, rollback procedure, and approval owner.
- The plan preserves `nova.yazelix.com` as Nova's permanent host and identifies any provider limitation affecting future independent apex/Eon publication.
- The dependent deployment issue requires no unresolved provider, authority, or host choice.

## Stop Conditions
- Stop for the user if DNS/account ownership cannot be verified.
- Do not move DNS, enable hosting, or create workflows in this decision issue.
- Reject a provider choice that requires Nova to launch at the apex first.
- Do not design portability layers for a replaceable static host.

## Maintenance
- Effort: XS.
- Risk: MEDIUM because domain cutover affects the public site.
- Confidence: HIGH that credible static providers can serve the permanent Nova subdomain.
- Replacement cost: low if provider-specific code is limited to one deployment file.

title: Publish Yazelix Nova at nova.yazelix.com
description:
## Why
The repository is not the product until a verified candidate is served at Nova's permanent canonical host, `https://nova.yazelix.com`. Release needs an explicit static publication, `nova` DNS/TLS cutover, and rollback proof without using the apex as a temporary host.

## Evidence
- `astro.config.mjs`, `public/robots.txt`, `README.md`, and `docs/site_shape.md` currently name `https://yazelix.com`; the content/metadata dependencies must correct those inputs before release.
- The Astro build emits static HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Pagefind, sitemap, and `404.html`.
- No repository deployment configuration currently exists.
- On 2026-08-08, the apex returned a parked page rather than repository content.
- The hosting decision owns provider, trigger, credentials, DNS, TLS, rollback, and confirms support for the permanent Nova subdomain.

## Release Boundary
- This issue launches **Yazelix Nova** directly at `https://nova.yazelix.com`.
- That host is permanent; there is no Nova-at-root phase and no later Nova canonical-host migration.
- This issue does not publish an apex family page or Yazelix Eon.
- Deferred issue `yazelix-site-activate-yazelix-family-domains-v8d` may later activate the apex and `eon` hosts independently, without changing Nova.

## Scope
In:
- Implement the chosen provider's smallest supported static deployment path.
- Build from the exact candidate revision with bounded permissions, trigger, timeout/concurrency, and artifact retention where hosted automation is required.
- Configure the `nova.yazelix.com` DNS record, custom-domain binding, and TLS without unnecessarily changing the existing apex state.
- Refuse a candidate whose site config, canonical/social metadata, sitemap, robots, or public copy still identifies bare `https://yazelix.com` as Nova's canonical host.
- Validate core routes, sitemap/robots, 404 behavior, Pagefind search, assets, and canonical URLs on production.
- Record candidate revision, build/deploy observation, DNS/TLS state, and rollback proof.

Out:
- The future Yazelix family landing page, Yazelix Eon site, Nova host migration, apex redirect scheme, backend services, analytics, preview fleets, deployment abstractions, multi-region architecture, or unrelated repository automation.
- Promoting or modifying the canonical Yazelix runtime repository.

External contract:
- `https://nova.yazelix.com` serves the exact accepted static candidate over valid TLS and remains Nova's canonical origin; missing routes return the intended 404 experience; a failed cutover can restore the prior known-good Nova artifact without changing hosts.

## Implementation Notes
- Use the provider-native deployment mechanism chosen by the decision issue.
- If GitHub Actions is selected, use one deterministic build/deploy workflow with least permissions and concurrency cancellation; do not add a matrix.
- Capture existing DNS records before mutation and add the narrowest `nova` record required.
- Do not create redirects for a temporary apex launch that never occurred.

## Verification
- Clean install plus `bun run check`, `bun run build`, and `bun run test:e2e` at the exact candidate revision.
- Inspect built output: canonical URLs, social URLs, sitemap, and robots use `https://nova.yazelix.com`; no Nova canonical points to bare `https://yazelix.com`.
- Production HTTPS checks on `nova.yazelix.com` cover `/`, all core docs routes, `/features/`, the chosen Blog behavior, `/sitemap-index.xml`, `/robots.txt`, representative media, Pagefind search, and an unknown route.
- Confirm certificate hostname/chain, no mixed content, expected cache behavior, and the deployed source revision.
- Exercise or document rollback without destroying user data or changing the permanent canonical host.
- Confirm the apex remains outside this release except for any unchanged pre-existing state.

## Stop Conditions
- Stop if hosting/DNS authority or a launch-gating dependency is unresolved.
- Stop before changing DNS unless the user or named release owner approves the cutover.
- Stop if the provider cannot bind valid TLS directly to `nova.yazelix.com`.
- Do not call a source-tree build or provider preview a production launch.

## Maintenance
- Effort: S.
- Risk: HIGH during DNS cutover; LOW after static hosting stabilizes.
- Confidence: HIGH after the decision and launch gates close.
- Replacement cost: low when deployment remains provider-native and static.
